claim_text: RAGO achieves up to a 2× increase in QPS per chip compared to RAG systems built on LLM-system extensions.
cited_span: Our evaluation shows that RAGO achieves up to a 2x increase in QPS per chip and a 55% reduction in time-to-first-token latency compared to RAG systems built on LLM-system extensions.
label: supported
label_rationale: cited_span states the 2x QPS-per-chip figure directly.

claim_text: RAGO achieves up to a 55% reduction in time-to-first-token latency compared to RAG systems built on LLM-system extensions.
cited_span: Our evaluation shows that RAGO achieves up to a 2x increase in QPS per chip and a 55% reduction in time-to-first-token latency compared to RAG systems built on LLM-system extensions.
label: supported
label_rationale: cited_span states the 55% latency-reduction figure directly.

claim_text: In RAG vs. GraphRAG's evaluation, only about 65.8% of answer entities appear in the constructed knowledge graph for HotPotQA.
cited_span: In Appendix C , we show that only about 65.8% of answer entities appear in the constructed KG for HotPotQA and 65.5% for NQ, highlighting the sensitivity of KG-based retrieval to graph construction quality.
label: supported

claim_text: On the MultiHop-RAG dataset, 13.6% of queries are GraphRAG-only.
cited_span: For example, 13.6% of queries are GraphRAG-only, while 11.6% are RAG-only on MultiHop-RAG dataset.
label: supported

claim_text: On MultiHop-RAG with Llama 3.1-70B, the Integration strategy improves the best baseline by 6.4%.
cited_span: For instance, on MultiHop-RAG with Llama 3.1-70B, the Selection and Integration strategies improve the best baseline by 1.1% and 6.4%, respectively.
label: supported
label_rationale: cited_span attributes 6.4% to the Integration strategy specifically (1.1% is Selection's, not claimed here).

claim_text: GraphRAG leads to substantial improvements in comprehensiveness over a conventional RAG baseline for global sensemaking questions over datasets in the 1 million token range.
cited_span: For a class of global sensemaking questions over datasets in the 1 million token range, we show that GraphRAG leads to substantial improvements over a conventional RAG baseline for both the comprehensiveness and diversity of generated answers.
label: supported
label_rationale: cited_span names comprehensiveness explicitly as one of the two improved dimensions.

claim_text: Under the tested configuration, cluster-based chunking did not outperform simpler chunking strategies.
cited_span: Under the tested configuration, cluster-based chunking did not outperform simpler strategies.
label: supported

claim_text: No single chunk size consistently outperforms others across all mediums tested.
cited_span: However, no single chunk size consistently outperforms others across all mediums.
label: supported

claim_text: In RAGO's evaluation, hyperscale retrieval can spend over 80% of latency on retrieval.
cited_span: For instance, hyperscale retrieval can spend over 80% in retrieval (§ 5.1 ) while in long-context scenarios, retrieval accounts for less than 1% of the total latency (§ 5.2 ).
label: supported
label_rationale: cited_span states the 80% figure for hyperscale retrieval directly.

claim_text: RAGO achieves up to a 3× increase in QPS per chip compared to RAG systems built on LLM-system extensions.
cited_span: Our evaluation shows that RAGO achieves up to a 2x increase in QPS per chip and a 55% reduction in time-to-first-token latency compared to RAG systems built on LLM-system extensions.
label: unsupported
label_rationale: cited_span reports 2x, not 3x; the magnitude was changed.

claim_text: In RAG vs. GraphRAG's evaluation, only about 65.8% of answer entities appear in the constructed knowledge graph for NQ.
cited_span: In Appendix C , we show that only about 65.8% of answer entities appear in the constructed KG for HotPotQA and 65.5% for NQ, highlighting the sensitivity of KG-based retrieval to graph construction quality.
label: unsupported
label_rationale: cited_span attributes 65.8% to HotPotQA, not NQ; NQ's own figure in the same span is 65.5%. The dataset entity was swapped.

claim_text: Cluster-based chunking never outperforms simpler strategies, under any configuration.
cited_span: Under the tested configuration, cluster-based chunking did not outperform simpler strategies.
label: unsupported
label_rationale: cited_span is qualified to 'the tested configuration'; the claim drops the qualifier and generalizes to 'any configuration'.

claim_text: RAGO causes up to a 55% increase in time-to-first-token latency compared to RAG systems built on LLM-system extensions.
cited_span: Our evaluation shows that RAGO achieves up to a 2x increase in QPS per chip and a 55% reduction in time-to-first-token latency compared to RAG systems built on LLM-system extensions.
label: unsupported
label_rationale: cited_span reports a latency reduction; the claim inverts the direction to an increase.

claim_text: RAGO achieves up to a 2× increase in QPS per chip compared to RAG systems built on LLM-system extensions.
cited_span: Correct predictions exhibit deeper reasoning paths, more distributed evidence flow, and a more structured local connectivity.
label: unsupported
label_rationale: claim is true of 2503.14649v2 (see draft-01), but is attributed here to 2605.14192v1; the cited_span from that paper is about attribution-graph structure and says nothing about QPS or serving throughput.

claim_text: GraphRAG reduces end-to-end query latency by roughly 40% compared to standard RAG on multi-hop question answering benchmarks.
label: unsupported
label_rationale: no span in 2404.16130v2's abstract or cached HTML body mentions latency at all (verified: zero occurrences of "latency" in the extracted body text); the paper's own reported improvements are comprehensiveness and diversity, not speed.
